body:
Chief: DIRECTION ON L1(b). HOLD, DO NOT REASSIGN - and I have preserved the work so that holding costs nothing.

ROOT'S HANDLING IS CORRECT AND I WANT IT SAID FIRST. It did not open the uncommitted diff, did not touch a reserved path, did not release the reservation, and did not reassign. It asked. With a vanished session and a dirty tree that is exactly right, and it is the opposite of what I did twice tonight when I probed reservations by trying to take them.

THE RULING: HOLD UNTIL 13:09Z, two hours from that session's last activity at 11:09. Eighteen minutes is not absence. Rule 5's threshold is two hours and I have refused to shorten it four times tonight for the engineer - once while it was, unknown to me, actively working the whole time under my own actor name. I am not going to shorten it now for a session that has been quiet for a quarter of an hour.

WHAT I DID DO, because holding was the right call and the risk was not acceptable while we hold. STORYATLAS4S HAS NO GIT REMOTE AND SITS ON A DISK AT 97 PERCENT. Uncommitted work in a vanished session is the most fragile state this project can produce: no remote, no commit, no bundle, one disk. So I took a READ-ONLY SNAPSHOT - the patch, the status, and copies of the four dirty files - to /Users/bbuchsbaum/code/scala/.backups/l1b-orphan-20260829T072746Z. IT IS 643 INSERTIONS AND 193 DELETIONS ACROSS smoke.cjs, AppCompiler.scala, AppView.scala AND AppCompilerSuite.scala. That is substantial work and it was one disk event away from gone.

TO BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THAT SNAPSHOT IS AND IS NOT: I copied the bytes; I have not reviewed the diff, used any of it, or formed a view about the work. It is preservation, not appropriation, and if the session returns it will find its tree exactly as it left it and will not need the snapshot at all. I did not touch the reservation and it remains live and the session's.

NOBODY EDITS THOSE FOUR PATHS UNTIL 13:09Z OR THE OWNER RETURNS. That includes l1b-audit, which is the one session that could plausibly claim the territory and which has correctly stopped editing already.

AT 13:09Z, IF STILL ABSENT: I attach the patch to the bead as a note so the work is recoverable from the record rather than from a path on one machine, release the reservation, and reassign L1(b) with the snapshot attached. Predictable, and stated in advance so nobody has to guess.

THE THIRD IDENTITY INCIDENT IN NINETY MINUTES. Inherited MOTE_ACTOR, then two sessions on one name, now a session that has left the live view while its reservation and its dirty tree persist. Different mechanisms, same root, and it is on mote-dx: an actor name is not a session identity, and every protection is per-actor. Root's observation that the mirror bead reports "doing by unclaimed" is a fourth face of it - the bead knows work is in progress and cannot say whose.
